source: Payoff-ordering strategies and minimum-payment conventions for the Debt Calculator.
confidenceNote: Minimum-payment formulas vary by issuer; 2% or $25 is a common convention, not a universal rule.
note: SPEC.md Section 13 — minimum payment formulas vary by issuer (typically 1-3% of balance, or a flat floor, whichever is greater) and must not be hardcoded to one formula. A user-entered statement minimum always wins over anything derived here. Strategy definitions live in this file so adding one is a data edit, not an engine change.

minimumPayment.note: Used only when the user has not entered their actual statement minimum. Revolving accounts can be derived; instalment loans cannot, because the payment depends on the original term, which we do not ask for.

rules.note: 2% of the balance or $25, whichever is greater — a common issuer convention, not a universal rule.
Depends on the original term and amortisation schedule. Ask the user rather than inventing one.

Money borrowed from family or a friend has no statement and usually no interest: the minimum is the balance spread evenly over the months until the agreed pay-back date. A typed monthly amount still wins. D-124

strategies.label: Avalanche
strategies.blurb: Highest interest rate first. Costs the least in total interest.

strategies.label: Snowball
strategies.blurb: Smallest balance first. Costs more, but clears accounts sooner — which is what keeps people going.

strategies.label: Convenience
strategies.blurb: Whatever you most want gone — money owed to family, a debt tied to someone you'd rather not owe. Tag them and they go first.

strategies.label: Hybrid
strategies.blurb: Clear anything small enough to finish quickly, then switch to highest-rate-first.

emotionalPriority.note: Ranking for the convenience method. A debt with no tag sits at 0.

tags.label: Owed to family or a friend
One I'd rather not think about
Tied to someone I'd rather not be tied to

limits.note: 50 years. A simulation that hits this is reported as never paying off at the current payment, not truncated silently.
